_meta.purpose: Prompt-shape registry for route-intent.sh. Names one candidate agent from the roster so the session model can dispatch instead of doing mechanical work inline.
_meta.fire_rule: Fires only on a high-confidence tier match, outside cooldown, on a prompt longer than min_prompt_chars, with no exempt pattern matching. Silence is the default.
_meta.tie_break: A prompt matching several tiers resolves to the MOST capable matched tier, in escalation_order. Routing too low produces work that must be redone.
_meta.pattern_syntax: Values are regex fragments, matched case-insensitively against the scrubbed prompt (code fences, inline backticks, URLs, and XML bodies removed).
_meta.imperative_shape: A bare verb (\brefactor\b) fires on discussion as readily as on instruction - 'do not refactor it', 'i hate the redesign we shipped', 'should we refactor this'. Verbs in the opus_executor tier therefore require an IMPERATIVE shape: the verb sits at a clause boundary (string start, sentence punctuation, or after and/then/now/also/next), optionally behind a 'can you' / 'please' softener, AND takes a determiner-led object. Note the softeners are INSIDE the optional group rather than boundary tokens of their own - as boundary tokens, 'please' matched mid-clause and let 'should we please refactor the parser' through. Keep any new bare verb to the same shape; this is the most expensive tier to route to by mistake.
_meta.bounded_quantifiers: Every {n,m} here must stay BOUNDED. route-intent.sh scrubs quoted XML with a backreference, which defeats the engine's prefix optimization; an unbounded gap made a 156 KB paste take 14.9s against a 5s timeout.

exempt: \b(what do you think|your thoughts|thoughts on|does that look right|is that right|am i right)\b
nudge: ROUTE CHECK: this prompt reads as {label}. {agent} ({model}) could field it. Dispatch if the work is longer than the dispatch overhead; answer directly if it is not. Your call either way.
